_comment: INTEGRATIONS_FILE (design section 11). Nothing secret lives here in a real deployment — a shared secret carries a file path, not a value. Every reference an owner may write in a policy resolves through this file, so no owner ever writes a URL or a credential the gateway will use. A dangling reference is a boot failure that names both the ref and where it is used, rather than a request that fails months later.
_egress: Design section 5.3, as revised in v1.4.0 — see openspec/specs/egress-governance. `egressAllowlist` is RETIRED: a file still declaring it is a boot failure, deliberately, because ignoring it would leave an operator trusting a list nothing reads. Egress is allowed by default and forbidden two ways: these ranges, and the per-host deny rules an administrator states in the portal under Trust → Blocked backends. Rules are the half that changes; ranges are the half no portal action can widen.
_denyCidrs: Applied AFTER DNS resolution, to every URL an owner writes — a backend, a spec import, an MCP or A2A discovery document. IPv4 only, by construction (shared/net.ts); an IPv6 literal host is refused outright wherever a URL is written, rather than admitted past a range that could never match it. The control plane also denies its own PUBLIC_URL origin without being told.
_denyCidrsLocal: THIS IS THE LOCAL COPY AND MUST NOT BE DEPLOYED. Loopback is absent so the demo's backends, MCP server and A2A agent on 127.0.0.1:90xx are reachable. The image carries this same file at /app/config.sample/ as a sample to edit, not as a default it mounts: add "127.0.0.0/8" before deploying, or a backend is any process inside the container. RFC1918 is deliberately absent and should stay absent: this estate's backends are internal, and denying 10/8, 172.16/12 and 192.168/16 would refuse almost every legitimate binding. Deny a narrower internal range here if your estate has one.
_xml: Design section 5.1's `always` block for the soap variant. These are ceilings, not policy: no route setting turns them off, and DTDs, entities and processing instructions are refused outright rather than expanded safely.
_xmlMaxBytes: maxBytes bounds a *parsed document*: the WSDL and its XSDs at import time, and — since D12', which retires the original D12 — a SOAP body the gateway validates against those schemas. It is still not the request-size limit: an unvalidated soap route streams its body and is bounded by validate.always.maxBodyBytes like any other, so raising that for large posts does not require touching this.
_validationCeilings: Design section 8.4. The bounds a route's own `validate` unit may not exceed, so one API cannot spend the whole gateway's memory or CPU on validation. minSampleRate stops warning mode being switched off by setting a rate of zero and calling it observed. maxIncludeBodyExcerptBytes is 0 by default deliberately: a validation log line that quotes the body is a log line that carries whatever was in the body.
_tlsExceptionMaxDays: Design section 5.4. The longest a TLS exception may be created or renewed for. Renewing is a decision somebody makes again; a long expiry is a hope.
_clientCaBundle: Informational only — the platform does not read this bundle, the reverse proxy does. It is recorded so the governance report can say how wide `auth.mtls` with acknowledgeCnOnly actually is: a common name is unique only within one issuer.

clientCaBundle.description: Corporate issuing CAs trusted by the edge proxy for client certificates
issuers: CN=Example Corp Issuing CA 2, O=Example Corp

_issuers: Vetted token issuers. `auth.jwt`'s issuerRef and `auth.introspection`'s issuerRef each resolve to exactly one of these, so an owner chooses an issuer by name and never writes a JWKS URL. algorithms is an allowlist and is required: without one, a token signed with an algorithm nobody vetted would be accepted. An issuer needs a jwksUrl, an introspectionUrl, or both — one with neither can verify nothing. Commented out here because the demo stack registers no real issuer; copy the block up to enable it.
_tokenProviders: Vetted OAuth2 token endpoints for `backendAuth.type: oauth2-client-credentials`. The gateway fetches and caches the token; skewSec is subtracted from expires_in so a token is refreshed before it is refused rather than after.
_hmacSchemes: SaKeyLite (design section 5.5): the per-environment application id and key a backend expects. Two refs rather than two values, for the same reason as everything else here.
_sharedSecrets: Named secrets, referenced by every credentialRef above and by `auth.basic`. Use `file` for anything real — an inline `value` is for local development and puts the secret in this file. A ref that resolves to nothing is a boot failure, not a runtime surprise.
